title: Account Momentum — QBR Deck Builder and Renewal Tracker
summary: A modular QBR deck template and accompanying renewal tracker focused on 'Account Momentum' — designed to surface adoption signals, revenue runway, risk triggers, and specific expansion/renewal asks. Includes two variants (Standard and Enterprise) and a lightweight implementation checklist for CSMs to assemble a tailored deck in under 45 minutes.
audience: Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Renewal Managers, Customer Success leadership
objectives: 1) Make it fast to build QBRs that prioritize forward-looking momentum; 2) Provide a renewal tracker aligned to QBR asks and timelines; 3) Built-in call-to-action templates (expansion, renewal, exec intro) to increase conversion and alignment.
deck_structure: Cover — Account Momentum QBR | Customer name & date | Prepared by CSM
Executive Snapshot (1 slide) — 90s summary for execs: ARR impact, MRR change, primary ask, renewal window
What Success Looks Like (1 slide) — Customer goals mapped to product outcomes with success metrics (adoption KPIs, latency/cost wins, time-to-value)

Momentum Signals (2 slides) — Positive signals (usage growth, feature adoption, successful rollouts) and concern signals (drop in active seats, latency incidents, mounting support cases) — quick red/amber/green status
Customer Story & Use Cases (2 slides) — Vignettes of recent wins, screenshots or anonymized metrics, impact to teams and users
Operational Health (1 slide) — SLOs, incident summary for period, outstanding technical blockers and next steps
Economics Snapshot (1 slide) — Unit economics improvements, cost-per-inference trend, committed vs actual usage, ROI highlights
Renewal & Expansion Plan (1 slide) — Timeline, contractual milestones, recommended SKU or capacity changes, and resource ask (training, onboarding support)
Risks & Mitigations (1 slide) — Ranked risks with short mitigation plan and owner
Call to Action — Clear asks for the customer (renew, pilot new feature, commit to POC) and internal asks (exec intro, SRE support, discount approval)
Appendix — Deep dive metrics, raw charts, and linked tickets/PRs for technical stakeholders
slide_templates: Executive Snapshot template: single KPI tile layout — Top left: ARR delta, Top right: Renewal date + probability, Middle: 3-line narrative, Bottom: Primary ask (button style)
Momentum Signals template: two-column table with metric, trend sparkline, owner, and last action taken
Economics Snapshot template: small table for unit cost, tokens per request, aggregate monthly token consumption, and estimated savings from recommended changes
Risk matrix template: 2x2 grid (impact x likelihood) with quick mitigations and owners
renewal_tracker_template_variants: Standard Tracker (lightweight): columns = [Account, ARR, Renewal Window, CS Owner, Renewal Status, Last Touch, Next Action, CTA], view = table, cadence = 30/60/90 day notes

Enterprise Tracker (detailed): columns = [Account, Contract ID, ARR, Seats, Last Executive Meeting, Renewal Date, Negotiation Stage, Legal Owner, Finance Contact, Risks, Discount Approved (Y/N), Competing Vendors, Action Owner, Next Milestone Date], includes color-coded risk flag and linked artifact column for Confluence/Jira IDs
sample_ctas: Renewal-first CTA: 'Lock in committed capacity for next 12 months to maintain current unit pricing' — recommended to use when usage is predictable
Expansion CTA: 'Pilot Redwood Dedicated for high-throughput inference on 2 GPUs' — includes a 60-day POC offer and success criteria
Exec Intro CTA: 'Schedule 30-minute exec sync to unblock procurement and prioritize roadmap items' — attach agenda and ROI one-pager
implementation_checklist: Pull last 90-day usage trend and compile top 3 momentum signals
Run economics calc using Redwood Optimize baseline and attach to deck
Book internal prep call with SE to align on technical blockers
Draft renewal ask and alternatives (list of packages/pricing scenarios)
Attach legal and procurement deadlines to the Renewal Tracker
Send draft deck to customer for pre-read 3 business days before QBR
roles_and_responsibilities: CSM: assemble deck, own narrative, present CTA
Solutions Engineer: validate technical slides, prepare appendix artifacts
Renewal Manager: update tracker, lead negotiation calls
Customer Success Leadership: approve discounts and executive asks
measuring_success: Define 3 success metrics per QBR (e.g., renewal probability uplift, committed ARR delta, number of expanded seats). Track quarter-over-quarter conversion and time-to-closed for asks made in the QBR.
common_objections_and_replies: Objection: 'We need better unit economics before committing' | Reply: 'Recommend locking current price with staged capacity bumps; Redwood Optimize recommendations attached with estimated savings.'
Objection: 'Security/compliance gating the Dedicated deployment' | Reply: 'List of required artifacts and a 6-week phased plan for Private deployment readiness; propose an exec-to-legal sync.'
Objection: 'We prefer to re-evaluate post-PoC' | Reply: 'Define clear PoC success criteria and tie renewal incentives to outcomes.'
references: Internal: CS playbook v2 (Confluence) — link in linked_artifacts
Template examples: archived QBR decks folder
Product: Hosted API pricing sheet and Dedicated capacity brochure
notes: Working draft intended as modular building blocks — keep slide count tight (10-12 max) for executive meetings; use appendix for detail. This doc intentionally biases toward forward momentum and clear asks so CSMs leave meetings with a next step (renewal or expansion).
